svg.title: Norman Control: Castles, The Harrying of the North & Domesday Book (1066–1086)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 7 historical GIS atlas map of Norman England, the Welsh Marches, the Scottish Frontier, and unpartitioned Ireland (1066–1086), showing Berkhamsted and the White Tower in London, the land-clipped Scorched-Earth Harrying of the North zone from the Humber to the Tees across Yorkshire (1069–70), Norman coastal and Welsh Marcher castles including Portchester and Pevensey, and Winchester with the Great Domesday Book survey (1085–86).

g.text: Castles, Northern Terror, Frontier Keeps & Domesday

text.tspan: Motte-and-bailey castles & stone keep awe London
Villages & crops burned in Yorkshire; ~100,000 starve
Norman fortresses guard Channel coast & Welsh border
Royal officials record every manor, plough & taxpayer

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 7 ENQUIRY: MEDIEVAL ENGLAND (1066–1381)
Norman Control: Castles, Harrying of the North & Domesday (1066–1086)
Just 10,000 Normans controlled two million Anglo-Saxons through 500 castles, frontier earldoms, and scorched-earth terror in Yorkshire.
By 1086, William’s Domesday Book recorded every manor and taxpayer—proving Norman barons had seized over 80% of English land.
